Theme

Work & responsibility

master noun

a skilled craftsman; an expert in an art

also master craftsman, past master, a master of, masterly, mastery

classical

Liv. 42.3: reponendārum nēmō artifex inīre ratiōnem potuit (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 5.12 (Lewis & Short)

artifex, artificis m.

noun, third declension

a master of an art, a skilled craftsman

One who has mastered an art, from ars and faciō; Lewis & Short sets it against opifex, the worker in the humbler crafts. It also means an artist or performer (artificēs scaenicī), and, of a person, a past master at something, even at mischief. For the one who does it for a living, see professional.

Other words

  • magister, magistrī m. — a master, the one in charge; a teacher

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Col. 1.18: magister operārum, an overseer (Lewis & Short); Cic. de Or. 1.244: puerī apud magistrōs exercentur (Lewis & Short)

    The head of something (a ship, a company, a feast, a team of workmen) and the teacher of a skill: so the master with apprentices, who directs and teaches. Its everyday sense is teacher (see teacher); for mastery of the skill itself, artifex.

  • opifex, opificis m. — a craftsman, an artisan

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.150: opificēs omnēs in sordidā arte versantur (Lewis & Short)

    The maker in a manual craft; with a word for the craft, a master of it: opifex verbōrum (Cic. Tusc. 5.34).

Examples

  • Sed assuēscere oportet: nēmō nāscitur artifex.

    But you have to get used to it: nobody is born a master.Erasm. Coll., Lūsus puerīlēs, Natātiō, I 44 (not classical)

  • reponendārum nēmō artifex inīre ratiōnem potuit

    no master builder could work out how to put the tiles backLiv. 42.3 (Lewis & Short)

See also professional, craftsman, skill, teacher, master.
